body:
Code looks good to me.

I think this makes sense, but I expect there will still be some lingering issues with `Engine.time_scale = 0` outside of physics. Simpler projects probably won't run into them, but as soon as you rely on more engine subsystems like navigation, networking, audio and so on, it would be more likely that you'd run into issues.

Note that a time step of 0 is not a no-op with Jolt, as it will do maintenance on its broad phase even when passed 0, as seen here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e0603aeda3ce0e15c5843f5202172a56f3ff5534/thirdparty/jolt_physics/Jolt/Physics/PhysicsSystem.cpp#L147-L163

So theoretically at least, with this change, if you pause the game using `Engine.time_scale` and start adding a bunch of bodies, physics query performance will deteriorate until you step with a non-zero timestep again. You can also technically (until #107951 is fixed) crash under certain circumstances, but that's a bit more far-fetched.

In general this change makes me a bit nervous though, as `JoltPhysicsServer3D::step` does more than just step the simulation, and since you're not doing an early return in `PhysicsServer3D::flush_queries` (which you arguably shouldn't) you may or may not end up with some strange issues now that one will not always be followed by the other.

I can't speak to whether the same might be true for Godot Physics.

Anyway, I would ask that you leave `JoltPhysicsServer3D` out of this change for now, if you just need to get the Godot Physics part merged. I've been careful not to divide by a zero timestep in that module, so everything should work fine with a time scale of 0 when using Jolt.
